Printmade Apparel — Standard Operating Procedure

Order Processing:
Ready for Operations Coordinator

SOP-OPS-001
Version 1.0
Updated June 2026
Role Operations Coordinator
Systems Printavo • Zome CMS • Gmail
1

Overview & Trigger

This SOP covers the full order processing workflow triggered when an order is marked Ready for Operations Coordinator in Printavo. It applies to all order types: Printmade in-house, Zome (embroidery contractor), or split orders involving both.

Example Order
Invoice #6263 — Vogue Coffee Bar, Hats Summer 2026. One in-house line item (heat press) and two Zome line items (embroidery). Used as the working example throughout this document.

When an order is ready you’ll see the red READY FOR OPS button in Printavo at the top of the invoice. That’s your trigger to begin.

Printavo — READY FOR OPS button is your trigger to start processing

2

First Steps: Print & Read

1
Print two copies of the packing slip
  • Copy 1 — Your working copy. Write notes and checkboxes on this one.
  • Copy 2 — Customer copy. Set aside for local pickup or any in-house production items.
2
Read the Production Notes on the invoiceThis tells you who is producing what before you do anything else.

Scroll to the top of the invoice in Printavo. The Production Notes section lists which line items go to Zome and which stay in-house with Printmade.

Printavo invoice #6263 — Production Notes at top show who produces what

Example — Invoice #6263 Production NotesPrintmade: Youth Foamie: Vinnie design
Zome: Embroidery: Vogue Rainbow
Zome: Embroidery: Vogue Mountain
3

Label the Order & Set Up Your Tracking Sheet

Line Item Groups

Each group in Printavo = a distinct decoration setup. Groups going to different contractors are processed as separate purchase orders. On your working copy:

  • Label each Zome group A, B, C in order
  • In-house (Printmade) items get no letter — tracked separately
GroupLabelExample — Invoice #6263
In-houseNo letterHeat Press, Youth Foamie Vinnie design [PRINTMADE]
Zome group 1AEmbroidery: Vogue Rainbow, Rora Shasta Nylon, Deep Teal, 20 pcs [ZOME]
Zome group 2BEmbroidery: Vogue Mountain, Rora Shasta Nylon, Salmon, 20 pcs [ZOME]

Check for Existing Art Numbers

Look in each Zome line item description for a ZDA-XXXXX number.

  • ZDA number found → No new art request needed. Check that box as complete.
  • No ZDA number → Submit a new art request through Zome CMS.
Example
Group A (Vogue Rainbow): ZDA-43800 already in description → no new art request needed
Group B (Vogue Mountain): no ZDA number → new art request required

Write Your Tracking Checklist on the Packing Slip

For each line item group, write these checkboxes on your working copy and check them off as you complete each step.

Example packing slip — tracking checkboxes written in for each line item group

4

Critical Sequence — Always Do This Order

ImportantOrder goods BEFORE sending the Zome email. If a garment is out of stock or needs a color sub, you’ll need to update Zome anyway. Get goods confirmed first.
1
Order all goods from supplierRora, Decky, etc.
2
Log the cost of goods as an expense in PrintavoPayments/Expenses tab → + Expense. Category: Goods.
3
Submit Zome art request (new design) — OR confirm existing ZDA number
4
Send order email to Zome (Lauri)
5
For in-house items: create Production Kanban Card + schedule with Printmade team
5

Ordering Goods & Logging Expenses

Identifying the Supplier

The garment name and item number in each Printavo line item tell you which supplier to use. If you’re ever unsure, check the Google Wholesale bookmark in your browser — all Printmade wholesale accounts are listed there. A more detailed wholesale accounts reference document will be available in the Sales folder once created.

SupplierCommon Items
Rora (Aurora)Hats — Rora Shasta Nylon, Rora Olympic, etc.
DeckyYouth Foamie, Richardson hats, specialty caps
Ninja TransfersHeat transfer material for in-house decoration

PO Number Format

Enter the Printmade PO number in the purchase order field on the supplier’s website.

Order TypeFormatExample
In-house onlyPAC[invoice#]PAC6263
Zome Group APAC[invoice#]APAC6263A
Zome Group BPAC[invoice#]BPAC6263B

Spoilage Extras

There’s no hard rule — use your judgment. General guidelines:

  • Simple order, one color, straightforward decoration → extras may not be needed
  • Complex artwork or decoration → yes, order extras
  • Large runs (100+ pcs) → 5–10% overage is a reasonable buffer
  • When in doubt, ask Rachel before placing the order
Example
Invoice #6263:
Heat press (Youth Foamie) — ordered +2 extra Decky hats
Embroidery groups A & B — ordered +1 extra hat each
Note the overage on your packing slip.

Logging the Cost of Goods in Printavo

After placing the order, log what you paid as an expense on the invoice. This is how Printmade tracks cost of goods and monitors margins per order. Zome invoices also get logged here as Contracted Labor.

1
Go to the invoice in Printavo → click the Payments/Expenses tab
2
Click “+ Expense”
3
Set Category to “Goods” and enter the amount and a brief descriptionExample: Hats - rora, -$314.61
4
Save

Payments/Expenses tab — Payments/Expenses tab highlighted, + Expense button, and logged goods expense row

Why this mattersTracking both goods costs and contracted labor costs here lets Rachel see real margins on every order at a glance. Always log expenses promptly after ordering.
6

Submitting a Zome Art Request (New Designs Only)

Skip This Section IfThe line item already has a ZDA-XXXXX number. Only complete this for line items with no existing art ID.

6.1 — Access the Zome CMS

1
Click CMS in your browser bookmarks bar
2
Click “View Artwork Request Form”
3
Click “Create Artwork Request” — top right, green button

Zome CMS home — View Artwork Request Form highlighted

Artwork Requests list — click Create Artwork Request (top right)

6.2 — Fill Out the Top of the Form

New art request form — key fields highlighted

FieldWhat to Enter
CustomerPRINTMADE (autofills contact details)
Artwork NicknameClient name first, semicolon, then artwork name
Example: Vogue; Vogue Mountain Embroidery
Sales RepRachel Mozzetta (autofilled — leave as-is)
Statusnew (default — leave as-is)
Art TypeEmbroidery or Screen — only these two are used

6.3 — Set Dates

Date FieldRule
Due Date3 business days from today
Ex: submitted Monday → due Wednesday
Production Due DateCheck the Zome scheduling calendar (bookmarked). Find the next available date.
Art Completion DateLeave blank — do not fill this in

Dates section — green fields fill in, Art Completion Date leave blank

6.4 — Location Information

1
Click “Add Additional Item” under Location InformationOnly needed if there is more than one decoration location. This order has one location only.
2
Set Location to match the proofe.g., Full Front for a centered hat design
3
Set Number of Colors from the proof
4
Set Decoration Type to Embroidery or Screen
5
Enter thread/ink colors in Ink Colors fielde.g., White, 1372
Tip
Open the production proof in Printavo to confirm location, color count, and thread colors before filling in this section.

Location Information — Add Additional Item, Location, Ink Colors, and Decoration Type fields highlighted

6.5 — Quantity, Notes & Order Associations

  • Number of Units — match the invoice quantity (not including spoilage extras)
  • Notes — leave blank unless there’s a special instruction
  • Order Associations — leave blank (Zome internal use only)

6.6 — Upload Files & Save

Two files must be uploaded for every new art request:

  • Production proofs PDF from Printavo
  • Adobe Illustrator art file (.ai) from the client’s folder
1
Confirm file type is set to “Artwork Request”
2
Upload the proofs PDF → click “Save and Generate PDF”
3
Upload the .ai file → click “Save and Generate PDF” again
CriticalClick Save and Generate PDF after EACH upload — not just at the end.

File Options — file type, Save and Generate PDF button, and upload field all highlighted

6.7 — Capture the ZDA Number

After completing both uploads and saving, the ZDA-XXXXX number will appear in red in the top right corner of the form. This is generated only after the files have been uploaded and saved.

1
Find the ZDA-XXXXX number in red — top right of the form
2
Write it on your working copy packing slip
3
Go back to Printavo and add it to the line item descriptionThis enables fast reorders — no CMS search needed next time
4
Check the CMS box on your tracking checklist

Completed art request — ZDA number in red top right, only visible after files are uploaded and saved

7

Sending the Zome Order Email

7.1 — Use the Gmail Template

1
Open Gmail → Templates → Contract Order Form
2
Fill in all blanks using the table below

Gmail Contract Order Form template — subject line and shipping type fields highlighted

7.2 — Fill in the Email Fields

FieldWhat to Enter
ToLaurie at Zome
Subject LineNew Order PAC[invoice#][group letter]
Example: New Order PAC6263B
NicknameExact match of Artwork Nickname used in CMS
Example: Vogue; Vogue Mountain Embroidery
Shipping TypeBlind Ship, UPS V744J0 — always this exact text
Shipping AddressCopy/paste from Printavo — never retype manually
Requested Production DateProduction due date from CMS
In Hand DeadlineLeave blank if no hard event deadline
Art Request #ZDA number (e.g., ZDA-45645)
OrderItem name: Color — Example: Rora Olympic; Salmon
Total PiecesQty + spoilage note — Example: 20 (+1 for spoilage/color testing)
Shipping FromSupplier name (e.g., Rora, Decky)
ProofsAttach production proof PDF

Completed Zome email — PAC6263B example showing all fields filled in

7.3 — Large Order Shortcut

For orders with many garments, colors, or sizes, attach the Printavo work order PDF instead of typing each item manually.

7.4 — After Sending

  • Check the Email box on your tracking checklist
  • Laurie will respond with a Zome invoice — review, approve, and pay promptly
  • Log the Zome invoice amount as a Contracted Labor expense on the Payments/Expenses tab in Printavo
8

In-House (Printmade) Production

For items marked Printmade in the production notes, order goods, order decoration materials, and create a Production Kanban Card so the job enters the in-house queue.

1
Order garments from supplierPO format: PAC[invoice#]
2
Order decoration materialsExample: heat transfers from Ninja Transfers
3
Log cost of goods in Printavo Payments/Expenses tabCategory: Goods
4
Fill out a Production Kanban CardInclude: invoice #, client name, item, qty, decoration type, due date
5
Place the Production Kanban Card on the whiteboard in the production area
6
Write a brief entry on the whiteboard under Upcoming JobsFormat: [Client] [item], [qty] pieces — under the relevant production type column
Example: “Vogue hats, 30 pieces” under Heat Press
Example
Invoice #6263 in-house item:
Decky #7010 Youth Foamie, Yellow/White/Yellow, 30 pcs (+2 extra)
Decoration: Heat Press (Vinnie design)
Goods from: Decky • Transfers from: Ninja Transfers

Whiteboard entry: “Vogue hats, 30 pieces” under Heat Press
9

Final Checklist

  • Two packing slip copies printed
  • Production notes read — contractor assignments confirmed
  • Zome line item groups labeled A, B, etc. on working copy
  • All goods ordered from correct suppliers with correct PO numbers
  • Spoilage extras noted on packing slip
  • Cost of goods logged as expense in Printavo (Payments/Expenses tab)
  • Zome CMS: art requests submitted for new designs (ZDA # captured + added to Printavo line item)
  • Zome CMS: existing ZDA numbers confirmed for reorders
  • Zome email sent to Laurie — one email per group (A, B, etc.)
  • Zome invoice received, approved, paid, and logged as Contracted Labor expense in Printavo
  • In-house: Production Kanban Card filled out and placed on production whiteboard
  • In-house: job added to whiteboard under Upcoming Jobs with production type
  • In-house: decoration materials ordered
  • Customer copy packing slip set aside for pickup or in-house production
